{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfy99XJ9MZ9MHy95TQzYp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The matmul benchmark now runs its multiply on the GPU through a CUDA kernel. The CPU loop is gone, and the executable is still `matmul`. Only `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt` changed, and I built in `/tmp` so the repo has no new files.\n\n**Results on an RTX 3090 (sm_86):**\n\n| N | GPU time | GFLOPS | CPU baseline time |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1024 | 5.6 ms | 384 | 7835 ms (0.27 GFLOPS) |\n| 2048 | 32.7 ms | 525 | — |\n| 4096 | 229 ms | 599 | — |\n\nValidation (`-v`) passes at every size I ran. The output hash matches the CPU baseline bit-for-bit at N=64, 100, 512, 1000, 1024. At other sizes the last bits differ, because the compilers apply FMA contraction differently. Sums agree to rounding, and the existing validation tolerance covers this.\n\n**Choices I made that you may want to review:**\n- **Kernel design:** a 64×64 output tile per block, 16×16 threads, a 4×4 register block per thread, and shared-memory staging along k. The k loop runs in ascending order, so each output accumulates in the same order as the original serial loop. Edge tiles are zero-padded, so any N works.\n- **What is timed:** the kernel plus a device sync. Host-to-device uploads and the copy-back are outside the timer, the way the CPU version had its data already in memory.\n- **Output format change:** time is now `Computation time: %.3f ms` instead of whole milliseconds, because the GPU run at N=512 finishes in under 1 ms and would otherwise print 0 ms and infinite GFLOPS.
